thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Multiple smart-routing failures detected for eu-west endpoints; high 5xx rate + model mismatch signatures. Triggered by DNS/edge propagation anomalies. Paging oncall now.
alice: I'm on it. seeing ~30% 5xx on /v1/generate for a subset of EU POPs. latency spikes too. request ids  r_44* cluster.
ben: Confirmed. Logs show requests routed to model variant `redwood/rw-small-1` for customers pinned to `redwood/rw-medium-2` in eu-west. That explains quality regression.
carol: How many regions impacted? are fallbacks kicking to another region or an alternate variant?
dave: It's localized to eu-west edge POPs that have stale DNS records pointing to old proxy pools. Smart-routing fallback policy then mapped those proxies to older model variant as a graceful degradation — but the variant mapping is incompatible.
alice: Paging notes: traffic surface, customer impact = higher error rates + degraded outputs. Some customers reporting hallucinations.
ben: root cause hypothesis: DNS RRset TTL drift + CDN cache retention meant a subset of edge nodes continued serving stale upstream endpoints after recent rollout. smart-routing fallback policy doesn't verify variant compatibility when choosing fallback.
carol: Reproduce: curl to affected POP shows backend host header pointing to `proxy-legacy-03.eu` which is still wired to rw-small-1.
dave: Nice catch. Should we flip fallback policy priority to region-local first? or pause smart-routing while we fix DNS?
alice: Immediate mitigation plan:
- 1) disable smart-routing policy for eu-west (force single compatible routing)
- 2) purge CDN/edge caches for eu-west POPs
- 3) revoke legacy proxy routing entries
- 4) notify customers and escalate to SEs for affected tenants
ben: I'll roll the smart-routing disable now (config change). Doing a canary disable first on 2 POPs.
deploy-bot: config-change: /configs/routing/smart-routing/disable eu-west canary by ben @ 2003456835 — succeeded on pop eu1, eu2
alice: observing immediate drop in 5xx for canary pops. good sign.
carol: initiating CDN purge command for eu-west:
```
POST https://api.cdn.local/purge
{
  "scope":"eu-west",
  "type":"edge",
  "targets":"/v1/*"
}
```
carol: purge accepted. started invalidation across ~18 edge nodes.
dave: also kicking off DNS rrset transaction to force updated A/ANY records TTL to 60s so stale caches expire faster:
```
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-eu
# add new A records / replace
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-eu
```
ben: rollback of fallback-policy code path to earlier version (pre-variant-fallback) queued, but prefer config toggle first.
alice: customer comms draft: "We experienced degraded model outputs and some errors in EU due to an edge DNS propagation issue that caused mismatched model variants. We've applied mitigations (smart-routing paused, edge cache purged) and are monitoring. We'll share postmortem." Ready to post to status.
dave: Noting an operational gap: fallback policy lacked model-compatibility guard. Add to followups.
carol: CDN provider (cdn-co) replied: some nodes had extended cache retention because of incorrect cache-control header on our purge calls. We're coordinating to force evict.
ben: Observability: set alert threshold lower, added a temporary dashboard filter to show variant mismatch rate per POP.
alice: Handoff to second oncall at 2003459000 — @dave take incident lead for next hour, I'll stay in loop for customer comms.
dave: Taking lead. checklist: monitor error rate, ensure DNS changes propagate, verify all POPs return to expected variant.
carol: Running cross-check script to verify model variant served:
```
for pop in $(cat pops-eu.txt); do curl -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" http://$pop/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"identify-model"}'; done
```
carol: Results: 16/18 POPs now serve rw-medium-2, 2 still on rw-small-1 — contacting edge ops to restart those proxies.
ben: Edge ops restarted proxies on eu-legacy nodes. Confirmed via logs, variant reconciled.
alice: Customer impact summary for status page: ~12 tenants affected, elevated 5xx rate peaked at 32% in eu-west for ~27 minutes, errors resolved within ~45 minutes after mitigations. No data loss.
dave: Next steps (post-incident):
- 1) Add variant-compatibility check to fallback selection logic
- 2) Improve DNS change rollout verification (health-check before retiring old rrset)
- 3) Validate CDN purge success end-to-end and add retry/backoff
- 4) Run tabletop for smart-routing failures
ben: I'll own 1). created ticket INF-8721.
carol: I'll own 3). ticket CDN-451.
alice: I'll draft postmortem and timeline. Assigning to incident-review for tomorrow.
dave: closing pager in 15 once metrics stable. thanks all.
incident-bot: Incident update: severity=P1 -> mitigated; monitoring. channel: #incidents-2003456789 for postmortem drafts.
alice: ack. will put notes in the postmortem doc and link to runbook changes. :white_check_mark:
